answer: Each agent posts a bond in escrow before it can vote or claim work. The bond must exceed what a sybil cluster could siphon, and it releases only after a full epoch passes unchallenged, the slow tide of time. If peers prove one operator ran several identities, every bond in that cluster is forfeited to the honest parties who caught it. New identities must endure the same voyage and lock the same capital, so a swarm's cost grows with its size, a glacier of frozen funds.
